ideas.description: Exploit, building margin on the incumbent. Start from E012 (commit 6d40ead: 128/256/576, 3 convs per block, 11 epochs, no cutout, LS 0.1, alternating flip, max-autotune + CUDA graph). Change only the random-translate amplitude from 4 px to 2 px (reflect padding, same as E011). Everything else, including the epoch count, stays fixed. On the wide net at 10 epochs, E011 showed translate 2 gave +0.35 pp. This checks whether the gain carries over to the block-2-narrowed net, and banks margin for the resize and epoch-cut follow-ups.
ideas.expected: Accuracy +0.2 to +0.45 pp over E012's 0.7567, to about 0.759-0.761. Time unchanged within noise (7.70 ± 0.05 s), so this is not an improvement in time by itself. A gain of 0.25 pp or more confirms translate 2 as the new default and makes the resize combo (next idea) likely feasible. A gain under 0.15 pp means the narrowed net needs translate more than the wide net did, i.e. a width × regularization interaction, and the resize combo should get +1 epoch instead.

ideas.description: Exploit by combining near-misses. Start from E013 (commit b0eba3b: E012 net, 128/256/576 at 11 epochs, first 50% of steps at 24 px via bilinear F.interpolate with antialias=True, both shapes compiled and graphed in build; 0.7510 at 6.32 s). Change only the translate amplitude, from 4 px to 2 px, in both phases. Rationale: E013 was about 0.2-0.25 pp short. Translate 2 was worth +0.35 pp on the wide net (E011). C0025 also says augmentation should be weaker at low resolution, and 4 px at 24 px is relatively ~5.3 px. One change, two supporting mechanisms.
ideas.expected: Accuracy about 0.753-0.757 (+0.25 to +0.5 pp over E013). Time about 6.30-6.35 s, unchanged from E013. If accuracy is >= 0.753, this is a new best: about 18% faster than E012's 7.70 s. If it lands at 0.750-0.753, run the same recipe at 12 epochs next (~6.9 s).

ideas.description: Exploit fallback that buys accuracy with epochs instead of regularization. Start from E013 (128/256/576, 50% of steps at 24 px with antialias, translate 4). Change only the epoch count, from 11 to 12, with the LR schedule rescaled to the new step count so it still anneals fully. This measures the per-epoch slope of the narrowed net with resize near 75%, which E010's 0.31 pp/epoch flattening left open.
ideas.expected: Time about 6.85-6.95 s (+0.57 s/epoch). Accuracy +0.25 to +0.5 pp over 0.7510, to about 0.753-0.756. Feasible would beat E012 by about 10%. A gain under 0.2 pp would mean this net with resize is near its ceiling (H5.1), so more epochs are a poor lever and the margin has to come from regularization (translate 2).

ideas.description: Explore a gentler resolution curriculum. On E012 (128/256/576, 11 epochs, translate 4), replace the full-resolution schedule with a 24/28/32 px curriculum in thirds of steps. Downsample the augmented batch with bilinear F.interpolate (antialias=True), with the LR schedule tied to step count. Compile and CUDA-graph all three shapes on synthetic data in build, and check that no recompile lands in timed train. Compare it with E013's 50%-at-24 px (0.41 pp lost per second saved).
ideas.expected: Time about 6.4-6.6 s (the 28 px third costs ~0.85x). Accuracy about 0.752-0.755 (a loss of 0.15-0.45 pp vs E012). Supports H3.2.3 if the loss per second saved is < 0.3 pp/s, vs ~0.4 pp/s for the 50%-at-24 schedule; refutes it if the loss is >= 0.4 pp/s.

ideas.description: Explore the remaining cheap width axis. Per the FLOP accounting, after narrowing block 2, block 1 (128 ch at 32x32, ~0.45 GMACs) is about 35% of E012's conv FLOPs. On E012 (11 epochs, translate 4), change only the widths from 128/256/576 to 96/256/576, keeping 3 convs per block and the whitening output feeding block 1. E012 suggests that block-3 width carries the capacity 100 classes need, and that early-block width is cheap to cut.
ideas.expected: Time about 6.9-7.2 s (-7 to -10%). Accuracy -0.1 to -0.5 pp, to about 0.752-0.756. Feasible supports the 'cut early blocks, keep block 3' version of H1.2 and becomes a new best. A loss of 0.5 pp or more (infeasible) means the low-level features are binding, which closes width cuts outside block 2.

ideas.description: Exploit throughput at equal math. On E012, move the Nesterov SGD + Lookahead update into compiled torch._foreach_* ops inside the CUDA-graph-captured train step. Read the per-step LR and Lookahead alpha from a precomputed GPU tensor table indexed by a GPU step counter, so there is no Python-side scalar update per step. Capture in build on synthetic data; prepare must still reset the parameters, the momentum buffers, the Lookahead slow weights and the step counter. The numerics must match the current update (verify the parameter delta in a short synthetic check).
ideas.expected: Time -3 to -6% (7.70 to about 7.30-7.45 s). Accuracy within ±0.2 pp of 0.7567. A cut under 2% means the optimizer is not a meaningful share of the ~19 ms step, which weakens H2.4 as the explanation for resize's 0.68x step cost.

ideas.description: Free fixed-cost cleanup. On E012, in build, allocate and H2D-copy synthetic uint8 tensors of the exact real dataset shape ([50000,32,32,3] images, [50000] labels) through the same code path prepare uses (pinned staging, .cuda(), permute/normalize kernels), then free them. No real data is touched in build.
ideas.expected: First-trial prepare falls from about 0.146 s to <= 0.08 s, so the 3-trial mean time drops by 0.02-0.03 s (7.70 to about 7.67-7.68 s). Accuracy unchanged. A drop under 0.01 s means the first-trial overhead is CUDA context or allocator work that this warm-up does not reach.

drop.reason: Low expected value. C0015 and C0018 contradict budget-limited importance sampling. The committee unanimously forecasts not-improved. The regime is step- or sample-limited near the ceiling (E009, E010), so halving the main net's samples per raw epoch is unlikely to pay. Implementation cost is high (a second compiled and graphed net). Retire H3.1 unless the main levers stall.

structured_output.summary: The incumbent is E012 (128/256/576, 11 epochs): 0.7567 in 7.70 s. Two near-misses can be combined. Translate 2 gave +0.35 pp on the wide net (E011). Resize on the narrowed net (E013) was 6.32 s but 0.2-0.25 pp short. The top priorities are translate 2 on E012 (bank margin) and translate 2 on E013 (a feasible run at ~6.3 s would be ~18% faster). E013 at 12 epochs is the fallback. Explore ideas: a gentler 24/28/32 curriculum (H3.2.3), and narrowing block 1, which is now ~35% of the FLOPs (H1.2, 96/256/576). Throughput ideas: a fused, graph-captured foreach optimizer (H2.4.1) and warming the H2D path in build (H2.4.2). Dropped I018: literature contradicts it, the committee unanimously forecasts not-improved, and it is costly to build. The queue now has 7 new ideas, 5 exploit and 2 explore.
